corfu.intro: Corfu's remarkable trees split into a town walk and three drives. In the old town an oak in the Liston has been pruned close to its limit, and an ombu in the People's Garden was registered purely for its strange shape. In Mon Repos park, three Moreton Bay figs stand near the tallest Aleppo pine in the Greek Tree Registry. Further out, a plane at Gastouri has a stone wall built against its trunk, a healthy giant elm shades the square at Strinylas, and at Panachori in the south an olive is reported at 21.66 metres round its base.
corfu.meta_description: Corfu's remarkable trees: an olive 21.66 metres round at Panachori, three giant figs in Mon Repos, a rare oak in the Liston and a big elm at Strinylas.
corfu.question_meta: No tree on Corfu has a measured age. The Saint's Olive at Panachori has the biggest trunk, and the 2,700-year figure told about it has never been tested.
corfu.question_answer: Nobody can say which tree on Corfu is the oldest, because none of these has a measured age. The strongest candidate by size is the Saint's Olive beside the church of Agios Spyridon Panachoritis at Panachori, in the south of the island, reported at 21.66 metres round its base. A local estimate repeated in the press puts it near 2,700 years, but no study has dated it, and the 2019 declaration that protects it gives no age.
corfu.question_context: Olives are the hardest trees to date, and Corfu's records do not help. The Panachori olive was declared a Preserved Natural Monument in 2019. Fighters from Argyrades swore oaths beside it in the war of 1716, and plague dead were buried there in 1816. The 2,700-year figure rests on a method used on Cretan olives, and no study has dated this tree. The other trees here have no ages either. The elm at Strinylas is given as about 350 years by two travel guides and 100 by a guest listing, a gap too wide to split. The Gastouri plane, the Liston oak and the Mon Repos figs have measurements from the Greek Tree Registry and no ages at all, and for the figs girth would not help, because their aerial roots fuse into new trunks and the registry warns that their size says little about age. What can be compared is size, and there the olive leads by a distance. If you know the age of any tree on this page, tell us.

faq.q: Can you see Corfu's old trees without a car?
faq.a: Partly. The Liston oak, the ombu in the People's Garden and the trees in Mon Repos park are all in or near Corfu town, and Mon Repos is about 35 to 40 minutes on foot from the Spianada. Gastouri is about 10 km south, with a local bus towards the Achilleion. Strinylas, on the slopes of Mount Pantokrator, and Panachori, about 20 km south, are much easier by car.

faq.q: Is the Liston oak in good health?
faq.a: No. When the Greek Tree Registry recorded it in October 2024 it had been pruned repeatedly by the municipality, its regrowth was weak, and the branches on the north and west sides were drying out. It was alive and declining.

faq.q: Why is the Gastouri plane's girth given two ways?
faq.a: A stone wall has been built against the trunk. The registry measures at the top of that wall, 12.78 metres, because it is a point that can be found again. The free trunk at chest height measures 7.70 metres.

kefalonia.intro: Kefalonia's great tree stands on the Omala plateau, inland from Argostoli, a short walk from the monastery of the island's patron saint. Tradition says Saint Gerasimos planted the plane himself and dug the well at its root. Its rings tell a measured story instead. A study presented in 2023 put it at about 448 years, counted from the outer wood because the trunk is hollow, and that study led to its declaration as a Preserved Natural Monument in 2024.
kefalonia.meta_description: Kefalonia's Plane of Saint Gerasimos on the Omala plateau: about 450 years old by ring count, hollow, by tradition planted by the island's patron saint.
kefalonia.question_meta: Kefalonia's oldest known tree is the Plane of Saint Gerasimos at Omala, put at about 448 years in 2022 by a ring study of its hollow trunk.
kefalonia.question_answer: The oldest known tree on Kefalonia is the oriental plane of Saint Gerasimos on the Omala plateau, estimated at about 448 years in 2022, roughly 450 today. The figure comes from a ring count of the outer wood, because the trunk is hollow.
kefalonia.question_context: The age comes from a dendrochronology study presented at the Panhellenic Forestry Conference in October 2023, at Loutra Aidipsou by a team of seven researchers, and Greek authorities used it the following year to declare the tree a Preserved Natural Monument. The island's tradition says something different in kind rather than in number. It holds that Saint Gerasimos, Kefalonia's patron saint, planted the plane and dug the well at its root. The ring count is an estimate, since the hollow centre is gone, and the tradition is a tradition, so neither is offered here as proof of the other. The tree is 5.37 metres round and 24 metres tall, recorded by the Greek Tree Registry in September 2024. It stands in an open square about 500 metres from the monastery gate, free to visit, and you need a car to reach the plateau. If you know the tradition as the monastery tells it, or anything the study left out, tell us.

faq.q: Did Saint Gerasimos really plant the plane at Omala?
faq.a: That is the island's tradition, and the ring count neither proves nor disproves it. What has been measured is the tree's age, about 448 years in 2022, counted from its outer wood.

faq.q: How do you get to the Plane of Saint Gerasimos?
faq.a: By car, inland from Argostoli to the Omala plateau. The tree stands in an open square about 500 metres from the entrance of the Monastery of Agios Gerasimos, with no ticket or gate.

paros.intro: Paros's remarkable tree is a cypress 35 metres tall in the Valley of the Butterflies at Petaloudes, about 7 kilometres from Parikia. The Greek Tree Registry counts it among the largest cypresses in Greece, and 22 metres away stands a stone pine it counts among the largest of its kind. The valley is a private reserve and a Natura 2000 site, home to the jersey tiger moth, open in summer for a small fee. The cypress can also be seen from the road.
paros.meta_description: Paros's giant cypress, 35 metres tall in the Valley of the Butterflies at Petaloudes, one of the largest in Greece, with a big stone pine beside it.
paros.question_meta: No tree on Paros has a known age. The biggest is the 35-metre cypress in the Valley of the Butterflies, one of the largest cypresses in Greece.
paros.question_answer: No source gives an age for any tree on Paros. The biggest is the Mediterranean cypress in the Valley of the Butterflies at Petaloudes, 35 metres tall and 4.45 metres round, which the Greek Tree Registry counts among the largest cypresses in Greece.
paros.question_context: The cypress grows on private farmland inside the Butterflies Nature Reserve, near the monastery of Agios Arsenios, in a valley of cypresses, ivy-covered planes and wild olives. Its neighbour, a stone pine 3.3 metres round and 22 metres tall, stands 22 metres away with ivy on its trunk. The registry recorded both in August 2026 and gave no age for either, and no other source does. The reserve opens from June to September, 10:00 to 18:00 according to the registry, and charges a small fee. Out of season the gate is shut, but the cypress is visible from the road. The valley is also part of the Natura 2000 network, as the site Paros: Petaloudes, and the reserve is home to the jersey tiger moth. The registry adds that butterflies live on the ivy of the stone pine. The reserve is about 7 kilometres from Parikia, the island's main port, by bus or car. If you know how old either tree is, tell us.

faq.q: Can you see the Paros cypress outside the summer season?
faq.a: From the road, yes. The reserve itself opens June to September, 10:00 to 18:00 according to the Greek Tree Registry, and the stone pine beside the cypress can only be seen from inside.

faq.q: How far is the Valley of the Butterflies from Parikia?
faq.a: About 7 kilometres by road, near the monastery of Agios Arsenios.
